claims.text: Low-cost option (with metformin, TZDs, human insulin) when cost is a barrier, weighing hypoglycemia and weight gain.
claims.quote: In adults with diabetes and cost-related barriers, consider use of lower-cost medications for glycemic management (i.e., metformin, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones, and human insulin) within the context of their risks for hypoglycemia, weight gain, cardiovascular and kidney events, and other adverse effects.

claims.text: Most patients on a sulfonylurea alone eventually need more medications.
claims.quote: Most patients taking sulfonylureas alone eventually require additional medications to achieve normoglycemia

claims.text: Glipizide ER 5 mg PO daily with breakfast (2.5 mg in elderly or hepatic insufficiency);
claims.quote: The recommended starting dose of GLUCOTROL XL is 5 mg once daily. Start patients at increased risk for hypoglycemia (e.g. the elderly or patients with hepatic insufficiency) at 2.5 mg
The maximum recommended dose is 20 mg once daily.

Treatment of patients with glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency with sulfonylurea agents, including GLUCOTROL XL, can lead to hemolytic anemia. Avoid use of GLUCOTROL XL in patients with G6PD deficiency.
All sulfonylureas promote hyperinsulinemia and weight gain of 2 to 5 kg

claims.text: Hypoglycemia risk: age > 65, long-acting agents (chlorpropamide, glyburide, glipizide), erratic eating/exercise, kidney or liver insufficiency;
claims.quote: Risk factors include age > 65 years, use of long-acting medications (especially chlorpropamide, glyburide, or glipizide), erratic eating and exercise, and kidney or hepatic insufficiency.

claims.text: with long-acting agents it may last days and can be fatal.
claims.quote: Hypoglycemia caused by long-acting medications may last for days after treatment cessation, occasionally causes permanent neurologic disability, and can be fatal.

claims.text: Label warning: possible increased CV mortality.
claims.quote: Potential Increased Risk of Cardiovascular Mortality with Sulfonylureas: Inform patient of risks, benefits and treatment alternatives
A potential interaction between oral miconazole and oral hypoglycemic agents leading to severe hypoglycemia has been reported
Concomitant treatment with fluconazole increases plasma concentrations of glipizide, which may lead to hypoglycemia

claims.text: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, fibrates, fluoxetine, MAOIs can increase hypoglycemia.
claims.quote: The following are examples of medication that may increase the glucose lowering effect of GLUCOTROL XL, increase the susceptibility to and/or intensity of hypoglycemia: antidiabetic agents, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blocking agents, disopyramide, fibrates, fluoxetine, monoamine oxidase inhibitors

claims.text: Beta-blockers, clonidine may mask hypoglycemia signs.
claims.quote: The signs of hypoglycemia may be reduced or absent in patients taking sympatholytic drugs such as beta-blockers, clonidine, guanethidine, and reserpine.
GLUCOTROL XL should be administered at least 4 hours prior to the administration of colesevelam.

claims.text: Teach patients to recognize and manage hypoglycemia.
claims.quote: Educate patients to recognize and manage hypoglycemia.

claims.text: Can promote weight gain; use judiciously at the lowest dose with obesity.
claims.quote: Insulins, sulfonylureas, and thiazolidinediones can promote weight gain and should be used judiciously and at the lowest possible dose.
claims.locator: Pharmacologic Therapy for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes

claims.text: Hypoglycemia from long-acting agents may last days after stopping; some clinicians hospitalize, especially older patients.
claims.quote: Hypoglycemia caused by long-acting medications may last for days after treatment cessation, occasionally causes permanent neurologic disability, and can be fatal. For these reasons, some physicians hospitalize hypoglycemic patients, especially older ones.
